To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the signaling pathways that are activated in T cells by antigen and by mitogenic stimuli are different.

(1) the expression of the T cell receptor complex is down-regulated in senescent T cells, and (2) the expression of T cell growth factor receptors is down-regulated and the expression of interleukin-2 receptors is up-regulated in senescence.

(1) the activation of lymphocytes is regulated by a series of transmembrane signaling events; and (2) the age-related reduction in lymphocyte function is related to deficiencies in the transmission of signals across the lymphocyte membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms involved in the activation of B lymphocytes.
the identification of the signaling molecules involved in the transduction of extracellular signals across the cell surface of lymphocytes.
the elucidation of signal transduction mechanisms in lymphocytes and their role in the regulation of the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immune response in the elderly is not as efficient as in the young.
immunosenescence is the result of a combination of intrinsic and extrinsic mechanisms that are still not completely understood.

the mechanisms of signal transduction in lymphocytes are complex, and that the nature and the sequence of the signals that are essential for lymphocyte activation and proliferation are not yet fully defined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the signaling mechanisms of the immune system are impaired during aging and this is due to the loss of the ability to generate second messengers and the inability to activate transcription factors.
the signaling pathways in lymphocytes are not affected by aging, however, the expression of the receptors and the response to the ligands are affected by age.
we have identified the signaling mechanisms involved in the activation of T lymphocytes and the role of these signals in T lymphocyte differentiation and proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are multiple mechanisms by which the immune system ages, and that these mechanisms are not independent of each other.

the age-associated reduction of immune function in the elderly is due to an impairment in the ability of the immune cells to receive, process, and transmit the signals that are essential for their activation and function.
there are many ways to skin a cat.
